messages:
alerts-bot: ALERT: us-chicago (ord3) control-plane egress flap detected. ~50% of gpu nodes in gpu-pool-ord3 showing NotReady + eviction surge. Severity: P1. monitoring.dashboard/ord3 | alert: ORD3_EGRESS_FLAP
jessica: Confirming. Dashboards show node evictions spiking at 12:02 UTC. 95th latency for serving up ~600ms. Customers seeing generation errors.
samir: Any BGP/TCP-level signals? Is this provider-level or our top-of-rack?
kai: Short logs show TCP resets to upstream next-hops in the pop. Example: 
```
TCP_RESET: 10.0.8.5 -> 198.51.100.23 RST, seq 0
Drop window: 12:01:56 - 12:02:10
```
Looks like intermittent upstream resets rather than internal kernel OOMs so far.
natalie: Starting triage plan: 1) soft-hold auto-eviction on gpu pools in ord3 2) stepwise traffic shift to us-west1 as overflow 3) open vendor escalation. Will coordinate steps and confirm.
ingrid: How do you want me to hold drains? I can flip node eviction annotation + pause autoscaler.
ingrid: run: 
```
kubectl annotate nodes -l pool=gpu-ord3 nodes.redwood.io/eviction=hold --overwrite
kubectl patch hpa gpu-pool-ord3 --patch '{"spec":{"minReplicas":2}}'
```
I can apply now.
samir: I'm pinging provider account rep + network-eng. Opening ticket with level3-net and sending syslogs. Vendor acked receipt.
level3-net: We see microbursts and BGP session resets in the ORD POP; investigating adjacent fabric. Will update in ~10m.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-438 created and paging oncall-sre, network-eng, and infra-leads. Linked to runbook: runbooks/ord3-egress-flap.md
jessica: :thumbsup: Starting traffic shift to us-west1 with a 10% step now. Monitoring token errors, tail latency, and GPU saturation.
kai: Note: west1 GPU pools are currently ~70% utilized. Large shifts will raise egress costs and risk saturation. Recommend 10% step + 3m observation windows. Also prepare to cold-start extra central capacity if needed.
natalie: Agreed. We'll do 10% step, wait 3m. Enable fallback models (smaller context) for non-critical workloads to preserve throughput.
ingrid: kube-controller logs: 
```
I0321 12:03:15 eviction_controller.go:145] Node gpu-ord3-42: eviction queued
I0321 12:03:22 network.go:88] egress write timeout to 198.51.100.23
```
This matches the reset windows.
samir: If provider can't stabilize inside 15m, plan B: spin up spot-style GPUs in us-central1 (lower perf) and start cross-region cold-start for serving fleets. Trigger if eviction rate doesn't drop below 5/min.
jessica: Noted. I'll coordinate with account execs for Dedicated customers impacted by capacity shifts.
level3-net: Update: we've identified a flapping interface on one of the upstream spine routers in ORD; applying mitigation config now. Monitoring for stabilization. ETA 10m.
ops-bot: Labels updated: region=ord3 severity=P1 impacted_services=serving,control-plane owner=jessica
natalie: Next actions: 1) hold evictions (ingrid) 2) execute 10% traffic step to west1 (jessica) 3) prepare central spot capacity (kai) 4) vendor escalate if not stable (samir) 5) update incident board (ops-bot).
jessica: Executing step-1 & step-2. Holding annotations applied, 10% shifted. Monitoring now.
level3-net: Update: we've pushed a config to stabilize BGP adjacencies. Metrics show a dramatic reduction in resets. Will continue to monitor 5-10m.
jessica: If we get a 10m healthy window we'll start reversing traffic and then run a controlled return. If instability returns we follow plan B. Keep updates coming in this thread.
